title: Microsoft Teams Rooms: proximity join for attendees of Teams events
summary: Hold: the briefing treats the published Teams Rooms Pro requirement for event attendees as unconfirmed merely because it does not name proximity join. The rollout, default and Bluetooth configuration are supported, but the licensing caveat needs correcting and the conflicting Windows and Android support statements need reporting explicitly.

claims.claim: Attendee proximity join in Teams events is planned for Teams Rooms on Windows.
claims.quote: Attendees can take advantage of proximity join with Teams Rooms on Windows and/or Android

claims.claim: Attendee proximity join in Teams events is planned for Teams Rooms on Android.
claims.quote: Attendees can take advantage of proximity join with Teams Rooms on Windows and/or Android

claims.claim: The roadmap names town halls, webinars and structured meetings as events in scope.
claims.quote: during Teams events, such as town halls, webinars, and structured meetings.

claims.claim: The change lets event attendees connect to nearby room systems with fewer steps.
claims.quote: This enhancement simplifies the meeting join experience and helps users connect to the appropriate room device with fewer steps.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The feature is on by default and becomes available automatically during rollout.
claims.quote: This functionality will be available by default as part of the Microsoft Teams Rooms experience.

claims.claim: Administrators need take no action to enable the feature.
claims.quote: No action is required to enable this feature. It will become available automatically during the rollout.

claims.quote: Targeted Release: Rollout will begin in early November 2026 (previously early October) and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and is expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously mid-November).

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.

claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Android, Desktop, iOS, Mac, and Teams and Surface Devices.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Teams and Surface Devices"]

claims.claim: Learn has no page specifically describing attendee proximity join in events at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "proximity join" "events" "attendees"; Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events town hall webinar. Opened rooms/proximity-join, rooms/teams-devices-feature-comparison and meetings-events-feature-comparison; no feature-specific description found.

claims.claim: General proximity join lets a user in the desktop or mobile Teams app invite or nudge a room into a meeting.
claims.quote: Proximity Join is a feature that lets end users use the Teams app on a desktop or mobile device to invite or nudge a Microsoft Teams Room into a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: Bluetooth is a documented wireless technology used by proximity join to discover nearby rooms.
claims.quote: Rooms discovered through Bluetooth are sorted by signal strength in descending order

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Ultrasound proximity join is available on compatible Windows consoles, not Teams Rooms on Android.
claims.quote: Ultrasound signaling is available on Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows (from compatible consoles). Proximity Join using ultrasound isn't currently available for Teams Rooms on Android.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that every detail of the general proximity join page applies unchanged to events.
claims.quote: Searched: "proximity join" "events" "attendees" and "proximity join" "events" "lobby". Opened rooms/proximity-join and meetings-events-feature-comparison; neither states all proximity join meeting details apply unchanged to events.

claims.claim: Learn requires Bluetooth enabled on both the room and desktop or mobile client for proximity to function.
claims.quote: Bluetooth must be enabled on both the Teams Rooms device and on the client desktop/mobile endpoint in order for proximity to function.

claims.claim: Proximity join requires no direct network connection between personal and room devices; communication goes through Teams.
claims.quote: Proximity join doesn't require a direct network connection between a user personal devices and the Teams Rooms device, all communication takes place through Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Bluetooth discovery signals can penetrate walls.
claims.quote: However, this signal can penetrate through walls.

claims.claim: Bluetooth-discovered rooms are sorted by descending signal strength.
claims.quote: Rooms discovered through Bluetooth are sorted by signal strength in descending order

claims.claim: Bluetooth discovery includes rooms both in use and not in use.
claims.quote: it includes all Teams Rooms both in use and not in use. This is because the Bluetooth signal isn't paused when Microsoft Teams Room has joined a meeting.

claims.claim: General proximity join nudges must come from the same tenant or a trusted external organisation.
claims.quote: Proximity Join nudges from a desktop or mobile client must come from a user within the same tenant or from a trusted external organization.

claims.claim: General proximity join fails when the participant cannot bypass the meeting lobby.
claims.quote: if the meeting participant using proximity join from their device is unable to bypass the Teams Meeting lobby, the proximity join will fail

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically described event proximity join rules for external and anonymous attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: "proximity join" "events" "lobby"; Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events tenant lobby. Read rooms/proximity-join and plan-events search excerpts; meeting nudge rules and event lobby rules are documented, but their event-proximity interaction is not.

claims.claim: Teams Rooms on Android Bluetooth use is limited to advertising beacons and prompted proximal connections.
claims.quote: Bluetooth technology use on Teams Rooms on Android devices is currently limited to advertising beacons and prompted proximal connections.

claims.claim: These Android proximity features do not pair Bluetooth devices.
claims.quote: There's no Bluetooth device pairing as part of these features.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no autonomous or AI action or room self-joining for this event feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms proximity join events attendee data room roster automatically join ultrasound Bluetooth. Read rooms/proximity-join, rooms/security and release-note excerpts; no autonomous event joining or AI mechanism described. MC1461157 describes user-initiated connections.

claims.claim: The attendee chooses to connect a nearby room when joining an event.
claims.quote: Users will be able to use proximity join to connect to nearby Microsoft Teams Rooms when joining Teams events.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described extra attendee or room data sent by proximity join specifically in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms proximity join events attendee data room roster automatically join ultrasound Bluetooth. Read rooms/proximity-join, rooms/security and release-note/room-audio troubleshooting excerpts; these describe meeting roster association, not extra event-specific data.

claims.claim: People or animals with sensitive hearing may hear ultrasound tones from Windows consoles.
claims.quote: People or animals with sensitive hearing may be able to hear the ultrasound tones.

claims.claim: Proximity join is included in a licence that Teams Rooms already requires.
claims.quote: The following tables compare the Teams Rooms Basic and Teams Rooms Pro licenses and show what features are available with each. Join Teams meetings with 1-touch, proximity, and meeting ID | ✔ | ✔

claims.claim: The general licensing table lists meeting proximity join for both Teams Rooms Basic and Teams Rooms Pro.
claims.quote: | - | Microsoft Teams Rooms Basic | Microsoft Teams Rooms Pro | ... | Join Teams meetings with 1-touch, proximity, and meeting ID | ✔ | ✔ |

claims.claim: A shared meeting device requires a Teams Rooms licence.
claims.quote: A device used as a shared meeting device requires a Teams Rooms license whether it participates by signing in to a Microsoft Teams client, by anonymous join, or by authenticating a Microsoft 365 identity

claims.claim: Enterprise per-user Microsoft 365 suite licences are not authorised for shared meeting devices.
claims.quote: Enterprise per user Microsoft 365 suite licenses aren't authorized for use on shared meeting devices in any of these configurations.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate licence specifically for attendee proximity join in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events licence Basic Pro pricing meter. Opened rooms/rooms-licensing and meetings-events-feature-comparison; they give general proximity entitlements and a Pro event requirement, but no separate proximity-in-events licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate meter or charge for attendee proximity join in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Rooms attendee proximity join events licence Basic Pro pricing meter. Opened rooms/rooms-licensing, rooms/proximity-join and meetings-events-feature-comparison; read roadmap and MC1461157; no event-proximity meter or charge stated.

claims.claim: The events comparison says only Teams Rooms on Windows with Pro are officially supported as presenters or attendees.
claims.quote: Only Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with a Pro license are officially supported to join meetings and events as a presenter or as an attendee.
claims.fix: Add after the quoted requirement: 'However, the same comparison table lists Teams Rooms on Android as able to join as an attendee or presenter, and MC1461157 names both Windows and Android for this rollout.' This explicitly reports the conflicting support statements rather than implying only the roadmap supports Android.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether the published Teams Rooms Pro event-attendee requirement governs proximity join.
claims.quote: Only Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with a Pro license are officially supported to join meetings and events as a presenter or as an attendee.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft has not said whether that statement governs proximity join.' Replace the licensing open question with 'How will Microsoft reconcile the comparison footnote requiring Windows with Pro for event attendees with its table and MC1461157, which include Android? Watch the meetings and events comparison and MC1461157.' The published requirement covers Windows Rooms joining as event attendees without excluding proximity join; do not present Basic event entitlement as merely an unaddressed join-method question.
